parsed.explicit_disagreement: The PR's own description claims the HARNESS_PROVEN vs CLOSED_LIVE distinction is 'encoded in executable/governance logic, not only prose'. I disagree: the distinction is encoded in the audit's verdict field and in the json_count_equals criteria, but the ACTIVE_TRACK gate does not enforce it — a track with 11 HARNESS_PROVEN loops can still show 30/30 green and only an INFO finding prevents SHIPPABLE. That is prose-plus-INFO, not a hard executable gate. To call this rock-solid, the gate itself must refuse SHIPPABLE while any loop is HARNESS_PROVEN.
required_changes: Add a hard governance gate (not just an INFO finding) that prevents loop-closure-2026-06 from flipping to SHIPPABLE while any loop is HARNESS_PROVEN rather than CLOSED_LIVE. Encode this in check_track_status.py or a new guard so the 30/30 green cannot be misread as production closure.

Refresh or remove the 2026-05-05 'Evidence From ~/.dharma/' section in CYBERNETIC_LOOP_MAP.md, or move it under an explicit 'HISTORICAL — superseded by latest_audit.json' header so stale numbers cannot be read as current live state.

Render the contents of bounded_replays and live_owner_surface_criteria in latest_audit.md (or link to the per-loop replay JSONs) so a maintainer can see what was actually exercised, not just that the keys exist.

Soften or remove the 'Immediately closeable when dispatchable_now() is non-empty' roadmap language in CYBERNETIC_LOOP_MAP.md, or label it explicitly as 'non-claim — illustrative only, not a closure assertion'.
In latest_audit.md, define 'live_registration' and 'manifest_registered' fields explicitly (what they prove and what they do not), or remove them if they are not load-bearing for the claim boundary.

In active_track_evidence.md, render the HARNESS_PROVEN/CLOSED_LIVE/BLOCKED verdict split prominently next to the 30/30 count for loop-closure-2026-06, not only in the findings list, so the boundary is visible at first glance.
parsed.summary: The PR materially improves the claim boundary: HARNESS_PROVEN vs CLOSED_LIVE is now encoded in executable governance (json_count_equals criteria on latest_audit.json, a One Wire guard test, and a guard receipt), and the audit doc explicitly states it is a read-only verifier. However, several weaknesses remain that prevent a 95+ score. (1) The ACTIVE_TRACK completion criteria for loop-closure-2026-06 still pass on file_contains/receipt_valid proxies against self-generated text — the same class of weakness the prior critique flagged. A maintainer reading the evidence file sees 30/30 green and could reasonably believe closure is achieved; the 'track-provisional' INFO finding is the only thing preventing SHIPPABLE, and that finding is buried in a findings list rather than enforced as a hard gate. (2) The CYBERNETIC_LOOP_MAP.md still contains a long 'Evidence From ~/.dharma/' section dated 2026-05-05 with stale numbers and a 'Last audit: 2026-07-02' header — a maintainer skimming the doc could read the 2026-05-05 numbers as current. (3) The audit's 'live_registration: True' and 'manifest_registered: True' fields are not defined anywhere visible; their semantics are unclear and could be misread as live-closure evidence. (4) The 'bounded_replays' key is required by the receipt_valid criterion but its contents are not surfaced in the markdown — a maintainer cannot tell from the audit doc what was actually replayed vs what was asserted. (5) The One Wire guard test passes (9/9) but the guard receipt's 'command_to_replay' and 'tests_run' fields are not shown in any human-readable surface, so the guard's strength is opaque. (6) The CYBERNETIC_LOOP_MAP.md 'Which Loops Close First' section still uses language like 'Immediately closeable when dispatchable_now() is non-empty' which could be read as a closure roadmap rather than a non-claim. (7) The active_track_evidence.md shows loop-closure-2026-06 at 30/30 with no visual distinction between HARNESS_PROVEN and CLOSED_LIVE in the evidence rendering — the count is correct but the rendering does not foreground the boundary.
